s1.syndrome_frame: obstructive uropathy with renal impairment in a newborn
key_facts: 36 weeks' gestation at referral
Suspected fetal renal anomalies
Prenatal ultrasound showed bilateral renal enlargement and hydronephrosis
Prenatal ultrasound showed a markedly dilated fetal bladder
Left perirenal fluid collection measured 64 × 34 mm
Emergency cesarean delivery
Male infant with stable vital signs
Normal physical examination
Elevated serum creatinine at 156.1 µmol/L
Postnatal MRI showed mixed T1 and T2 signals in the left perirenal collection
Magnetic resonance urography revealed bladder wall irregularity and thickening
Bilateral ureteral dilation and urinary retention

shortlist.label: Posterior urethral valves
shortlist.why_kept: Obstructive uropathy suggested by prenatal ultrasound and postnatal MRI findings

shortlist.label: Prune belly syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral renal enlargement and hydronephrosis, along with bladder wall irregularity and thickening

shortlist.label: Urethral atresia
shortlist.why_kept: Markedly dilated fetal bladder and urinary retention on magnetic resonance urography

shortlist.label: Congenital ureteropelvic junction obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral ureteral dilation and hydronephrosis on prenatal ultrasound

shortlist.label: Multicystic dysplastic kidney
shortlist.why_kept: Left perirenal fluid collection with mixed signals on postnatal MRI, suggesting renal dysplasia

raw.rationale: The prenatal ultrasound findings of bilateral renal enlargement and hydronephrosis, a markedly dilated fetal bladder, and oligohydramnios, combined with the postnatal MRI and magnetic resonance urography results showing bladder wall irregularity and thickening, bilateral ureteral dilation, and urinary retention, are consistent with the diagnosis of posterior urethral valves, which is a common cause of lower urinary tract obstruction in male infants.

rejected.label: Prune belly syndrome
rejected.why: While prune belly syndrome can cause renal anomalies and urinary tract issues, it typically presents with additional characteristic features such as absent or weak abdominal muscles, which were not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Urethral atresia
rejected.why: Urethral atresia would likely cause more severe oligohydramnios and pulmonary hypoplasia, which were not reported in the case.

rejected.label: Congenital ureteropelvic junction obstruction
rejected.why: This condition typically causes unilateral hydronephrosis, whereas the case presented with bilateral renal enlargement and hydronephrosis.

rejected.label: Multicystic dysplastic kidney
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a non-functioning kidney replaced by multiple cysts, which was not consistent with the imaging findings in the case.
